name: VariableProximity-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The bold swell lands mid-line, showing the thin-to-heavy gradient clearly.

tagline: Letters swell to bold wherever the pointer touches them.
summary: Two lines of a sentence sit on black, and each letter grows heavier and wider the closer the pointer comes, easing back to thin as it moves away.
appearance: Two centred lines of white type, one large and one smaller, sit on a black stage. Within each line some letters are broad and bold while their neighbours stay light and narrow.
behaviour: Wherever the pointer goes, letters within a certain radius thicken and stretch, strongest right under the cursor and fading outward. Moving away lets them return to a thin width.
demo_content: "Bring your cursor closer" over "and watch every letter respond".
search_phrases: letters get bold near the pointer
use_when: A display headline should feel alive and reward the pointer without moving from its place.
avoid_when: Paragraph text or touch-only screens: it needs a pointer and a variable font.
customise: The label, from and to font settings, radius, falloff curve, class names and a click handler are props. The page must load the variable font.
weight_why: An animation-frame loop restyles every letter as the pointer moves.

a11y.note: A hidden copy of the sentence serves screen readers, but there is no reduced-motion handling.

polish_why: Smooth weight changes and a clean two-line setting; the effect is subtle at a glance.
